segments.text: Listen to a talk in a history class.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: The Renaissance was a pivotal period in European history, spanning roughly the 14th to the 17th centuries.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: The Renaissance is characterized by a renewed interest in art, science, and literature.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: It marked a significant departure from the Middle Ages and laid the groundwork for the modern era.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: One of the defining features of the Renaissance was the revival of classical learning.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: Scholars and artists looked back to the texts and artistic achievements of ancient Greece and Rome for inspiration.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: This led to a flourishing of ideas and creativity, evident in the works of figures like Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo, and Galileo Galilei.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: The invention of the printing press by Johannes Gutenberg around 1440 was a crucial development during this time.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: It allowed for the mass production of books, making literature and scholarly works more accessible to a broader audience.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: This contributed to increased literacy and the spread of Renaissance ideas.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: The Renaissance also saw major advancements in science, particularly in astronomy.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: Nicolaus Copernicus proposed a heliocentric model of the solar system, placing the sun, not the earth, at the center.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: Galileo Galilei later used a telescope to observe celestial bodies, providing evidence that supported Copernicus's theory.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: These discoveries challenged long-held beliefs and laid the foundation for modern astronomy.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: Despite political instability in some regions, the Renaissance left a lasting legacy on European society.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: Its influence can still be seen today in art, science, and education.
